- **task-171 工具调用预算与收敛机制重构 — WS-0 前置核实结论 (2026-09-16, 已完成)**: 本轮把工具调用的主闸门从「轮次硬上限」倒转为「无进展检测 + token 预算」，轮次上限降级为保险丝、撞顶由判死改为优雅收尾。施工前三条前置事实已核实（不凭猜测施工）：
  - **(1) 租约额度语义 = 形态甲（恒定 `LeaseUses = 1`）**。`GovernanceService.ConsumeLeaseAsync`（`Governance/GovernanceService.cs:1084-1091`）唯一的扣减路径是在 `Status="active" && StartsAt<=now<ExpiresAt && UseCount < MaxUses` 条件下 `UseCount + 1` 的 CAS（`affected != 1` 即判 `lease_unavailable`，`:1092-1107`；用尽置 `exhausted`，`:1109-1111`）。生产消费入口只有两处：`Tools/ToolDispatcher.cs:304`（幂等键 `tool-lease:{execution.Id:N}`，`:312`）与 `Runtime/UserToolActionService.cs:461`（`user-tool-action-lease:{action.Id:N}`）；`TryConsumeLeaseAsync` 在生产代码里**零调用方**。**幂等键按 execution/action id 派生**，所以 `ResumeAsync` 每次 tick 都会再调 `ConsumeToolLeaseAsync`，但除首次外全部命中 `LeaseConsumptionRecord` 收据（`GovernanceService.cs:975-993`）直接回放旧决定、不再扣减 —— **一个执行恰好扣 1 次**，恢复/重放不会二次扣减。因此「一张票 N 次额度」本就是浪费，恒定 1 反而强化一次性 nonce 语义，且 `Lifecycle/ToolApprovalCoordinator.cs:1216` 的 `1..32` 校验与 `ToolDispatcher.cs:812` 的 clamp 天然通过、**保持不动**（不制造假缺陷面）。
  - **(2) 附带发现：`LeaseUses` 同时决定 grant 的额度预留**（同向收敛，非缺陷）。`GovernanceService.RequestPermissionAsync` 经 `ReserveGrantUsesAsync`（`:516`，CAS 在 `:1431-1449`）按 `RequestedUses = clamp(execution.LeaseUses,1,32)`（`ToolDispatcher.cs:812`）预留 `CapabilityGrantRecord.UseCount`；改恒定 1 会把每次执行的 grant 预留从 N 降到 1，与 lease 同向。**三套额度互不相同，勿混为一谈**：`CapabilityLeases.UseCount`（每 execution +1）、`CapabilityGrants.UseCount`（每 execution 预留 N）、`PreAuthorizationRecord.UseCount`（每 tool call +1，`Lifecycle/ToolApprovalCoordinator.cs:349-353`，`AspNetCore/ControlPlaneService.cs:542-550` 注释所指即此）。**审批路径不消费 capability lease**：`ToolApprovalCoordinator.DecideAsync` 只 CAS `ApprovalRequests` + 写决策记录；`TryStartAsync` 的一次性 CAS（`:671-695`，`ConsumedByExecutionId`）与 lease 无关。已登记观察：`ToolDispatcher.ResumeAsync` 的消费发生在 approval CAS **之前**，审批 CAS 失败时该次消费不回滚（额度被烧掉但不会被扣两次，且同 execution 重放仍会命中收据返回旧 allow）。
  - **(3) checkpoint 加 nullable 字段安全**。`FullDuplexCheckpointV1`（`DmaEA/FullDuplexRunEngine.cs:3431-3506`）与 `DurableTaskNode`（`:3514-3564`）的**读写两侧**都是 `new JsonSerializerOptions(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web)`（引擎 `:30`；投影侧 `DmaEA/RunReplayService.cs:55-60` 与 `AspNetCore/Endpoints/DmaeaEndpoints.cs:665` 显式对齐 camelCase/大小写不敏感/忽略未知成员），**两个类型上没有任何 `[JsonExtensionData]`/`JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`**：旧 body 缺新字段由属性初始化器兜底，新 body 多字段被旧读取方忽略。`FrozenConfigurationHash` / `FrozenRunConfigurationV1.ContentHash`（`DmaEA/FrozenRunConfiguration.cs:113-116`）与 `AgentRuntimeConfigurationSnapshot.ContentHash`（`DmaEA/AgentRuntimeConfiguration.cs:319`，只对 TOML 文本取 SHA256）**均不含 checkpoint 字节**；`DmaEA/RunFreezeGate.cs:37-83` 的 `Validate` 也不接触 checkpoint。唯一会变的是 `RunCheckpointRecord.ContentHash`（= checkpoint body 的 SHA256，写侧现算现存），而 `Lifecycle/StorageLifecycleService.cs:1059-1076` 的 `ReadMatchingCheckpointAsync` 只在**同 (run,lane,purpose,revision+1) 幂等键重放**时要求 hash 相同 —— 故**新字段（保持默认值、不写出）安全**，但**修改既有字段的输出条件/命名/顺序有风险**（会让同键重放的字节不一致而抛 `InvalidOperationException`）。另注三条：协调器的 admission checkpoint 用裸默认选项序列化（`DmaEA/FullDuplexRunCoordinator.cs:494-510`），读侧大小写不敏感仍能读回；`FullDuplexCheckpointV1.SchemaVersion` 是**只写不校验**的摆设；`RunFreezeGate.ValidatePool` 在生产代码里**零调用点**（池形状目前未被恢复路径校验）。
  - **(4) token 字段名 = `ModelUsage.TotalTokens`**（**不是** `TotalTokenCount`）。`ModelUsage` 是 TinadecCore 自有 record：`Abstractions/Ports/IModelProvider.cs:53-63`，属性 `InputTokens`/`OutputTokens`/`TotalTokens`/`CachedInputTokens`/`ReasoningTokens`/`AdditionalCounts`（全部 `long?`，序列化为 snake_case）。`DmaEA/Maf18RuntimeAdapter.cs:83-96` 的 `NormalizeUsage` 从 M.E.AI `UsageDetails` 映射，`:98-118` 的 `AddUsage` 逐字段累加且**双侧 null 才返回 null**（`:154-155`）——即 provider 未报 total 时该次调用的 total 会被跳过，run 累计 `TotalTokens` 可能**小于** `InputTokens+OutputTokens`；`CachedInputTokens`/`ReasoningTokens`/`AdditionalCounts` 是**独立维度、不计入 total**。`checkpoint.ModelUsage`（`FullDuplexRunEngine.cs:3468`）语义是 **run 级累计**（planner/worker/supervisor/meeting/压缩/推荐/策展/steward 全部 `AddUsage` 累加）。WS-3 的 run 级闸门据此读数，并登记「total 缺失时回退 `InputTokens+OutputTokens`」的取值口径为待实测校准项。
- **Tool dispatch/approval lifecycle repair (2026-09-09, Governance 39 / Architecture 11 / AgentFramework 126 / targeted Api classes green)**: eight confirmed lifecycle-layer bugs closed. (B1) Host-restart stale `running` executions no longer park on `already_running`: `ToolApprovalCoordinator.TryStartAsync` gained `allowStaleRunningReset` — a stale approval-gated running row converts to `outcome_unknown` (the consume CAS and the running mark commit atomically, so the approval was provably consumed; a mutating call is never replayed), a stale read-only running row is reset to `requested` and re-driven; `ToolDispatcher.ResumeAsync` short-circuits rows this process provably holds (new `Tools/InFlightToolCallRegistry.cs`) **before** the authorization phase can clobber their status back to `requested` — that clobber is why the coordinator-level guard alone was not enough. (B2) Provider handshake failure (`InvalidDataException`) and startup timeout (`OperationCanceledException` without caller cancellation) are contained as task-level failures with the new `RunErrorTaxonomy.ToolRuntimeUnavailable` category instead of escaping into the engine's run-level catch-all; host-stop cancellation keeps propagating unchanged. (B3) Run cancel interrupts in-flight wire calls: `TerminalSessionControlService.KillForRunAsync` (already invoked by run-control cancel) signals `IInFlightToolCallRegistry.CancelForRun`, and the dispatcher links that token into `CallProviderAsync` — mutating calls land in `outcome_unknown`, read-only calls become `cancelled`/`run_cancelled`. (B4) The wire timeout now covers the tool's own `timeout_ms` budget (+30s margin, clamp 1830s) so a 10-minute shell call is not killed by the 120s default (`ToolDispatcher.ResolveWireTimeout`). (B5) Shell-class embedded `success:false` results are recorded honestly without changing control flow: new `tool_executions.tool_success` column (nullable; bootstrap-reconciled like `lane_key`, no migration file), `ToolExecutionSnapshot.ToolSuccess`, `tool.execution.completed` payload `tool_success` + warning severity; the dispatch stays `completed` so the result still reaches the model. Open: the `GET /sessions/{id}/tool-executions` projection (AspNetCore, outside this change's scope) still needs to surface the flag. (B6) `shell` joined `AutoApproveOptions.HumanOnlyTools` (the registered command tool id; `command_run` kept). (B7) Approval expiry has an observer: `ToolApprovalCoordinator.SweepExpiredPendingApprovalsAsync` + a periodic pass in `RecoveryCoordinator` (`TinadecApproval:ExpirySweepEnabled` default true, `ExpirySweepIntervalSeconds` default 30) — live runs are enqueued so the existing park→`EscalateLaneAsync` path drives them to `awaiting_user` (the sweep deliberately does NOT mark their approvals, or the resume would hard-fail as not_approved); undrivable approvals (terminal or run-less) are expired directly. (B8) Risk vocabulary unified: `elevated` is formal everywhere and sorts medium < elevated < high (`GovernanceService.NormalizeRisk`/`RiskRank`, coordinator `NormalizeRisk`/`RiskRank`, dispatcher `RiskRank`, `AutoApprovePolicyRules.RiskRank`); unknown risk fails closed in the coordinator instead of coercing to medium; `AutoApprovePolicyRules.Engages` still refuses `elevated` at any ceiling (M8 invariant, pinned). New tests: `ToolDispatcherResilienceTests` (16), `ToolApprovalLifecycleFixTests` (6), Governance risk/human-only pins (`AutoApprovePolicyTests`, `GovernanceServiceTests.RiskVocabulary_ElevatedIsAccepted_UnknownRiskFailsClosed`).
- **Full-duplex engine hardening (2026-09-09, engine-side companion to the B-series; Api.Tests 252/252, AgentFramework 126/126, Governance 39/39, Architecture 11/11 green)**: five confirmed DmaEA-side bugs closed in `FullDuplexRunEngine`. (C1) The text/tool dispatch split now keys off the RESOLVED declaration surface instead of the planner's `required_tools` hint: both tick paths resolve every ready task through `GetWorkerToolsAsync` (instance grant ∩ frozen manifest), and an empty-`required_tools` task spawns its worker with the frozen template scope — concrete ids expanded against the run manifest and bounded by the parent instance's envelope, never a wildcard; dispatch stays scope/approval/budget-gated. The 3e8ff30 'empty required_tools → full authorized catalog' fallback was dead code (only reachable by tool tasks, which by definition have requirements), so a planner that emitted no `required_tools` doomed the task to 'not advertised' the moment the model improvised a catalog call. (C2) Every engine runtime status write goes through `TrySetRunStatusAsync` (reads the persisted state, skips transitions `RunStatusMachine` forbids, logs and swallows storage failures): a lane parking on an approval while another lane already waits `awaiting_user` is a legal coexistence and no longer throws the run into `FailRunAsync`; terminal writes (`failed`/`completed`) stay on the direct path. (C3) `PendingToolExecutionId`/`PendingToolApprovalId` are cleared whenever a task reaches a terminal state (`ApplyTaskResultAsync`, `FailedToolTask`, the park-expired escalation, which also annotates the orphaned turn with `approval_expired`), and every resume query filters terminal tasks via `HasLivePendingExecution`, so a failed/expired task is never resumed or re-evented on later ticks — including checkpoints written before the rule existed. (C4) The park-expired lane escalation is self-consistent and quiet: `EscalateLaneAsync` dedupes repeat escalations of an already-escalated lane, and the escalated-lane idle branch re-asserts `awaiting_user` every tick — the approval-decision cascade and dispatcher resume legitimately flip the run back to `executing`, and without the re-assertion an escalated run displayed `executing` forever. (C5) Worker resolution/creation configuration failures (required tool missing from the frozen manifest, frozen specialist without a version binding, persisted-assignment drift, spawn subset/budget refusal) are wrapped in `WorkerAssignmentException` and fail only their own task with `error_category:worker_assignment_invalid`; `WorkerUnavailableException` (no roster candidate) and a missing planner instance still fail the run by design. Regression E2E (five new `ToolChainEndpointTests` facts, in-process FakeToolProvider): `EmptyRequiredToolsTask_WorkerReceivesAuthorizedCatalog_AndToolCallDispatches`, `TaskRequiringToolOutsideFrozenManifest_FailsOnlyThatTask_RunCompletes`, `LaneEscalationWhileApprovalParked_DoesNotFailRun`, `FailedToolTask_IsNotResumedOrReEventedOnLaterTicks`, `ParkExpiredApproval_EscalatesLaneOnce_RunStaysAwaitingUser`. Harness additions: `ToolScriptedClient.WhenWorkerTurns`/`BeforeWorker`/`WorkerStarted`, `FakeToolProvider.FailOnCallNumber`, `ToolChainFactory` runtime-TOML knob. Known adjacents recorded for the lifecycle owner: `ControlPlaneService.DecideApproval` never enqueues the run when a *permission request* is rejected (the approval-row branch does), so a permission-parked run whose request is denied hangs until something else wakes it; and the `/runs/{id}/orchestration`+replay lane projections deserialize the checkpoint with bare `JsonSerializer.Deserialize` (no web options), so checkpoint-backed `lanes`/`task_keys` silently read as the default empty shape while event-derived data is fine.
- **Model configuration chain repair (2026-09-04, Api.Tests 212/212 green + live real-model verification)**: user-saved provider settings now survive and fail closed instead of drifting. (1) `ControlPlaneService.SaveProvider` merges the request body onto the persisted current-version config (`MergeProviderConfig`) instead of overwriting the whole blob, so Desktop partial writes (e.g. `putProviderModels` sending only `model`/`models`) keep `protocol`/`base_url`/`binary_path`/`launch_args`; an explicit JSON null clears a key. (2) `api_key`/`clear_api_key` are stripped before the config blob is stored — credentials live only in `ISecretStore` (the plaintext-in-content-store leak seen on 2026-08-27 provider versions can no longer be produced). (3) Deleting or disabling a provider still referenced by any live route's candidates returns `409 provider_in_use` (with route purposes); `?force=true` bypasses. (4) Provider/route PUT and DELETE are conditional updates: missing If-Match is `428 precondition_required`, stale revision is `412`; `ConnectCliRuntime` passes the row's live revision internally. Successful writes echo the new revision as an `ETag` header. (5) `DbContextSchemaBootstrapper.DropLegacyNotNullColumnsAsync` now drops NOT NULL columns the model no longer maps (index-referenced ones are left in place) — this fixed live databases where `model_route_versions.provider_id` (pre-f9c44c0 inline candidate) made every `SaveRoute` die with `NOT NULL constraint failed`, the deeper root cause of the 2026-08-26+ configuration-drift failed-run cluster (18 of 24 failures). Tests: `ControlPlaneConfigGuardTests` (12: If-Match 428/412, partial-merge retention, null-clear, secret never in blob, provider_in_use 409→force→readiness blocked, ready-path), `LegacyRouteSchemaReconciliationTests` (1), Gateway bun 44/44, Desktop vitest 332/332. Verified live on the developer instance: repaired AMD provider (key into SecretStore, blob clean), rebound chat/probe routes through the new If-Match API, `model-readiness` ready, and two real `DeepSeek-V4-Flash` conversations drove the full planner→worker→supervisor→meeting→evolution chain with 12/12 `succeeded` model invocations and `completed` runs.
- **Provider edit version collision repair (2026-09-09, Api.Tests 248/252 — 4 pre-existing git-commit E2E failures — + live end-to-end verification)**: `ControlPlaneService.SaveProvider` derived the new `ModelProviderVersionRecord.Version` from `provider.Revision + 1`, but `DevSeed` creates the seeded provider with `Revision = 0` alongside an existing **version 1**, so the first edit of any seeded/imported provider collided with the unique `(provider_id, version)` index and died with `SQLite Error 19: UNIQUE constraint failed: model_provider_versions.provider_id, model_provider_versions.version` → HTTP 500. Providers created through `POST /api/v1/model-providers` were unaffected (Revision and Version advance together), which is why the defect only appeared when editing the default seeded provider. Fixed by deriving `max(existing Version) + 1`, exactly the pattern `SaveRoute` already used; `SavePrompt` was checked and is self-consistent (it always increments both together, and no seeded fragment path exists). Regression test `ControlPlaneStorageTests.ProviderEdit_OnSeededRow_SucceedsAndIncrementsVersion` (two consecutive edits of the seeded row) — measured red with `Revision + 1` restored, green with the fix. Verified live against a fresh Core: seeded provider edit → revision 0→1, chat route rebind, `model-probe` ready, all four `model_*` readiness items ready, and a real `POST /interactions` run over the local model fixture streaming `ack → queued → ephemeral_agent → delta → done` with the assistant reply persisted. The 4 Api.Tests failures (`ApprovalFlowTests.UserToolAction_GitCommit_*`, `UnattendedLaneEndToEndTests.*_GitCommitWithoutHuman`) are pre-existing and environment-related (temp git repo has no HEAD); re-verified identical with this change stashed.
- The current Core tree contains 22 source projects (including the packable AspNetCore HTTP layer) and 4 test projects, including Governance and its contract tests.
- Shared storage is registered with four relational index tables and Core-owned file stores. Startup reconciles indexed events from valid JSONL records and reports an incomplete final JSONL line as a storage diagnostic.
- Model/provider/route, prompt fragment, agent, and approval projections are persisted with tenant/workspace isolation and immutable ContentStore versions. Provider credentials use the platform SecretStore and never appear in responses.
- **DmaEA invocation runtime — RETIRED route, kept as a historical record (2026-08-05)**: `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/invoke-stream` appended the user message (Desktop does not double-write), then ran the current planning (`PlanningAgent`) and execution (`ExecutionAgent`) agents over the `chat` model route resolved via `IChatResolver` (OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `ChatClientAgent` per task). The endpoint streams one terminal SSE chunk (`kind:done` on success, `kind:error` + `error_category:runtime` otherwise); it is request-bound, does not persist an assistant message, and does not provide delta/ack/usage chunks. The orchestrator persists `run.started`/`task_graph.created`/`task.assigned`/`step.result.created`/`run.failed` events plus task snapshots via `ILifecycleManager` (`UpdateTaskSnapshotAsync` bumps `TaskRevision`). `GET .../orchestration`, `.../tool-executions`, and `.../task-nodes` project from replayed events. `DevSeed` (in `Runtime/DevSeed.cs`, invoked from Api `Program.cs`) idempotently seeds a `chat` route + OpenAI provider (no API key stored) + `planner`/`executor` agents; without a stored key runs fail cleanly (`run.failed`, error chunk — never fake success). Failed runs keep `running` status for audit; only success completes.
- **Full-duplex runtime is implemented and tested**: `FullDuplexRunEngine` + `FullDuplexRunCoordinator` drive `POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/interactions` (the retired `invoke-stream` route is no longer an entry point) with idempotent client-message-id admission, `context_revision` snapshots and meeting context patches (supplement/goal_adjustment/status_query), governance coordination → task planning → execution → supervision → meeting finalization, worker spawn/lineage via `AgentInstanceService` (budgets from the frozen runtime profile), durable SSE (ack/delta/done/error) with replay/follow, run control (cancel/pause/resume), active-run limits, and restart recovery through leased checkpoints (`RunRecoveryHostedService`). `agent_instances`/`agent_candidates` projections and candidate review (`MemoryReviewEndpoints`) back the agent-evolution surface (`EvolutionEndpoints.cs`: generate/promote/reject, no longer 501). Tests use scripted chat clients (`FullDuplexEndpointTests`), temp-DB factories, and an empty v2 tool-manifest resolver.
- **Operation-layer trigger chain is wired (2026-08-29)**: `[triggers]` policy in `default-agent-runtime.toml` plus `DmaEA/Operations/OperationalTriggers.cs` evaluate frozen-roster operational roles at four engine anchors (task graph created, task completed, run finalized, capability missing) as bypass governance calls (never in the task graph, never user-visible, failures isolated as `operation.dispatch.failed`). context_compressor applies ToolCallAware-guarded `kind=compaction` CAS patches with `context.compacted` events; skill_recommender persists `checkpoint.RecommendedCapabilities` and injects them into replanning; the experience curator curates memory/agent candidates at run close under the `[memory]` allow-lists; git_steward emits advisory `git.steward.reviewed` only for runs that touched `git_*` tools. Workers may propose context patches via a `CONTEXT_PATCH: summary || content` line, arbitrated by CAS against the task's input revision. Non-status interactions get real meeting-model replies; FinalizeAsync re-checks cancellation around the meeting call. Promotion is no longer fail-closed: sanitize → publish immutable AgentVersion → record decision. MAF Workflows 1.18 was analyzed and deliberately not adopted (no distributed lease/approval hooks, no time-travel); the event journal is the replay medium (`RunReplayService`).
- **Tool chain wired end-to-end (2026-08-18, tests green)**: `TinadecToolsProcessManager` auto-probes `TinadecTools:ExecutablePath` (content root, then `TinadecTools/bin/{Debug|Release}/net10.0/`) when null, hosts one v2-manifest child process per workspace root on a BOM-free UTF-8 line-delimited JSON pipe (`new UTF8Encoding(false)` — `Encoding.UTF8` emits an EF-BB-BF preamble that corrupts the first JSON byte on the wire). `ToolManifestSnapshotResolver` freezes the authorized manifest per run; `ToolInvocationScopeResolver` verifies the frozen hash at resume; `ToolDispatcher` persists an execution before invoking the deterministic PDP, idempotently creates permission requests/leases, pauses in `awaiting_delegate`/`awaiting_user`, and only then creates a one-time ActionApproval for required writes. `ToolApprovalCoordinator` and `GovernanceService` enforce execution/run/task/agent/tool/parameter bindings, lease TTL/use limits, explicit deny and nonce consumption; decisions wake the run via `engine.EnqueueAsync(runId)`. `ToolChainEndpointTests` runs one full-duplex run→pending-approval→approve→resume→real `write_file` E2E through HTTP (approval stream stays open while pending; resume completes the same stream; `probe.txt` is really written); `TinadecToolsProcessTests` covers the real child process (5 tests). The TinadecTools project reference in Api.Tests is conditional (`Exists()` on the sibling monorepo path), and the four real-process entry points (`TinadecToolsProcessTests` plus the three `[RequiresTinadecToolsFact]` write-path tests) skip cleanly when the apphost binary is absent, so a Core-only showcase mirror builds and tests green without TinadecTools (`scripts/showcase/sync-showcase.ps1` excludes the process-test file from the mirror). `GET /api/v1/tool-layer-readiness` reports the real manifest and frozen-profile execution-agent scopes, degrading to warning notes when no default workspace root is configured. The generic `IToolProvider` contract is host-decoupled and verified by an in-process fake-provider E2E (`WorkerWriteFile_ThroughInProcessFakeProvider_DispatchLoopCompletesWithoutTinadecTools`): with `IToolProvider` replaced in DI, the full approval→resume→dispatch loop completes and Core never spawns the TinadecTools binary.
- **Multi-protocol chat support (2026-08-19, tests green)**: `ChatResolution` carries a `Protocol` value (`ChatProtocols`: `openai-chat` default, `openai-responses`, `anthropic-messages`). `ModelProvider.ResolveChatAsync` reads the provider config JSON `protocol` key and falls back to driver inference (`anthropic`/`claude` → anthropic-messages, `openai-responses` → openai-responses). `AgentChatClientFactory` (DmaEA, replaces `OpenAiAgentChatClientFactory`) branches on the protocol: OpenAI SDK chat completions, `GetResponsesClient().AsIChatClient(model)` (OPENAI001 experimental surface deliberately suppressed), or `Anthropic.SDK` 5.10.0 whose `MessagesEndpoint` implements `IChatClient` directly (base URL normalized to the SDK's `{version}/{endpoint}` format — a stored trailing `/v1` is stripped). `GET /api/v1/model-provider-templates` returns three protocol templates; `ToProvider` exposes `protocol`; `RefreshProviderModels` uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` headers for anthropic-messages discovery. No DB schema change — `protocol` lives in the immutable provider config JSON blob.

The full-duplex engine resolves and freezes the profile per run; the baseline orchestrator's legacy planning-layer selection and workspace overrides plus readiness diagnostic exposure were superseded by the 2026-08-27 agent-directory refactor below.

- **Generic Agent Pack + Office runtime closure (2026-08-25)**: `IAgentPackService`/`AgentPackService` and four `/api/v1/agent-packs*` endpoints validate SemVer, internal references, dual-layer topology, capabilities, RFC 8785/JCS digest and owner scope, then install Prompt -> Agent -> Mode -> eligible defaults atomically. Same version/hash is no-op, hash/resource/revision conflicts fail closed, lower bundled versions return `newer_installed`, equivalent legacy resources may be adopted, and custom defaults are preserved. `DevSeed` no longer writes Office Agent/Prompt/Mode/defaults; it retains only generic chat-route + planner/executor bootstrap. Mode snapshots pin exact AgentVersion/PromptVersion IDs and hashes; frozen prompts are assembled for meeting/planner/supervisor/worker, specialist selection is deterministic and fail-closed, assignment is persisted before invocation, and only meeting answers the user. The four dormant operation roles remain frozen without instances/events.
- **Composer modes wired to pack topologies (2026-08-26, Api tests 116 green)**: the bundled Office pack (**0.2.3** since the 2026-09-03 role-prompt closure; **0.2.1** since the 2026-08-31 permission closure; originally `0.2.0`) ships **7 modes** — `default-mode` (space.full_duplex full roster) plus `conversation.plan/spec/ask/vibe/auto/agent` whose node subsets mirror the TOML profiles' `operation_agents` and each carry that mode's legitimate worker subset (worker selection only sees the frozen roster of the active mode and fails closed without coverage). `POST /sessions/{id}/interactions` accepts `agent_mode` (plan|spec|ask|vibe|auto|agent): resolution order is explicit `mode_version_id` > latest published `conversation.{agent_mode}` version for the workspace > the session's existing mode; the resolved version persists via `UpdateSessionModeAsync` and admission runs under the `conversation` application semantics (`space`+`agent` stays the no-selection default). Unknown values return 400 `invalid_request`. `GET /api/v1/agent-modes/{id}` now returns the current topology for any live status — draft projection for drafts, published projection (+ `managed: true`) for published/pack-managed modes — so the Desktop canvas can render installed modes; the draft-only guard remains on update/publish writes. Gateway `sessionMapper` forwards `mode_version_id`/`meeting_model_override` (structured `{provider_instance_id, model}`; the legacy free-text `meeting_model` and split provider column were removed by the 2026-08-27 refactor), and `interactionsMapper` validates the `agent_mode` enum before passthrough.
- **Dual-layer permission closure (2026-08-31, Core 232 / Desktop 316 / Gateway 44 green)**: the operation/execution boundary is now permission data, not an engine habit. `Runtime/CoreAuthorizationContextResolver.cs` returns one unconditional `operation_layer_cannot_invoke_tools` deny for any `layer == "operation"` instance (so a pack-published `tool_scope: ["*"]` on meeting cannot authorize a governance tool call), and the `agent_version` boundary finally reads the key the writers use — `BootstrapAgentDirectory`/`AgentPackService` persist `tool_scope` while the resolver looked for `allowed_tools`, which left the immutable AgentVersion inert and let a broader frozen-roster copy re-widen a narrowed publish; the resolver accepts `tool_scope|allowed_tools|tools` and treats a declared scope as final (deny included), falling back to the frozen roster or instance definition only when no scope is readable. `FullDuplexRunCoordinator.FreezeToolManifestAsync` unions **only** `ExecutionAgents`, so a governance declaration no longer raises the run ceiling. `AgentInstanceService.SpawnAsync` refuses a wildcard child grant (`*` is a delegable envelope in published declarations only), which is what makes the per-instance `IsToolAllowed` gate a real boundary instead of one a planner could widen by typing `"*"`. `FullDuplexRunEngine.GetWorkerToolsAsync` now derives the model-facing declaration surface from `IFrozenToolManifestCatalog` (instance grant ∩ run-frozen manifest, self-checking the frozen hash) instead of re-reading the live provider manifest — that port finally has a consumer. `bootstrap-agent-directory.toml` declares `tools = []` for all six operation agents and the engine seeds meeting/supervisor/experience-curator from `definition.AllowedTools` instead of three hard-coded `[]` literals, and `GET /api/v1/tool-layer-readiness` derives every count from the resolved runtime snapshot instead of returning `Array.Empty` — measured live it still reports `agent_scopes: []` / `execution_agent_count: 0`, because `default-agent-runtime.toml` has carried no roster since 2026-08-25; exposing the *formal* per-agent scopes for the default workspace remains open. Tests (three new `[Fact]`s in `ToolChainEndpointTests`): `OperationLayerToolInvoke_IsDeniedByLayerPolicy_WhileWorkerIsAllowed`, `DerivedAgentCannotCarryWildcardToolGrant`, `AgentVersionBoundary_UsesDeclaredToolScope_AsFinalAnswer` — the last pins the `agent_version` mechanism, since the pack's frozen roster and its AgentVersion snapshot derive from the same data and therefore produce an identical answer today (latent, not exploitable). **Remaining wildcard, accepted by decision**: `worker.general` still declares `tool_scope: ["*"]` in the bundled pack — it is the only writable fallback worker in `conversation.vibe`, so narrowing it would make that mode's write tasks fail closed. It can no longer reach an instance regardless, because `SpawnAsync` refuses wildcard grants.
- **Agent terminal plumbing (2026-08-31)**: `Tools/TerminalSessionRegistry.cs` (in-memory projection of Core-admitted terminal sessions, keyed by `terminal_session_id` → run/task/execution/workspace) + `TerminalSessionControl.cs` (`ITerminalSessionControl.KillForRunAsync`, invoked by `POST /api/v1/runs/{runId}/control` when action=cancel) + `ToolEventPump.cs` (per-call channel that serializes provider wire events into the run event log without blocking the read loop). `TinadecToolsProcessManager` implements `CallStreamingAsync` + `WireEventBroadcast`; the read loop distinguishes event lines by the `"kind":"event"` marker before any `ToolWireResponseDto` parse. `ToolDispatcher` streams only for `ToolDispatcher.StreamingTools` (`shell`) and records the session from the tool result's `terminal_session_id`; broadcast events (post-call stdout of long-lived sessions, exits) are attributed back to the run by `TerminalSessionEventBridge`. Gateway-proxied endpoints outside the durable control-plane, DmaEA, and agent-evolution surface remain stubs: GET returns empty/default responses and unsupported writes return structured `501 capability_unavailable`.
- **M2 lane-aware main loop (2026-09-01, AgentFramework 78 / Api 157+1-known-flake green)**: behind the frozen `[orchestration]` switch (`lanes_enabled`, plus `max_lanes_per_run`/`max_tasks_per_lane` caps from the M1 lane model), `FullDuplexRunEngine.ExecuteReadyTasksAsync` ticks per lane instead of one global ready set: per-lane ready sets dispatch round-robin (main lane first) under the ONE global `Spawn.MaxParallelWorkers` budget. Cross-lane waits re-judge what used to be an unconditional `invalid_task_graph` failure into a parked lane (`checkpoint.Lanes[].Status="waiting"`, `task.Waits`, `orchestration.lane_waiting` event, `RunAwaitingExternalDecisionException` releases the lease so the recovery scan re-wakes the run), while genuine stuck states (crashed `running` task, in-lane unmet dependency chain, dangling dependency) still fail closed. A tool-awaiting lane parks the same way and resumes through the existing `PendingToolExecutionId` path. Checkpoint idempotency keys gained a lane segment (`run:{id}:{laneKey}:{purpose}:{rev}`) so two lanes saving the same purpose/revision can no longer collide onto one row and silently return the first body; an exact replay (same key, phase, content hash, expected revision, applied-through-sequence) still returns the stored row. At run terminal (complete AND cancel paths), `run_directives` queued while the run held the session are drained once — lanes-disabled runs append `orchestration.directive.rejected{code:"lanes_disabled"}` and mark rows `rejected`; lanes-enabled runs accept them for the M4 orchestration port (drain idempotence comes from the pending-status filter, not `DirectiveCursor`, which is only a count). New `ILifecycleManager` members: `ListPendingRunDirectivesAsync`/`DrainRunDirectivesAsync`, implemented by `StorageLifecycleService` (note: `run_directives.CreatedAt` ordering is client-side after materialization — SQLite rejects `DateTimeOffset` in ORDER BY) and delegated by `LifecycleManager`. E2E: `TwoLanes_WithLanesEnabled_RunCompletesWithBothTasks`, `RunTerminal_DrainsQueuedDirective_RejectedWhenLanesDisabled`, `LaneCheckpointSave_NeverReusesPriorRevisionBody`, plus 4 pure `CrossLaneWaitsFor` facts in `DmaeaLaneModelTests`. Honest gaps: the approval-parked lane-wait E2E waits on M3's scripted tool-approval harness (`ScriptedChatClient` has no tool-approval scripting); run status stays `executing` during lane waits (the run status machine has no `waiting` state — lane waiting lives only in `checkpoint.Lanes`); drained directives are marked accepted/consumed but not yet acted on (consumption = M4); the `/runs/{id}/orchestration` projection has no lane dimension yet (M6).
- **M3 cross-lane gate + per-criterion verdict (2026-09-01, AgentFramework 78 / Api 161+1-known-flake green)**: a lane whose cross-lane waits are factually satisfied no longer stays parked forever. `LaneWait` is now structured — `(LaneKey, Predicate, RequiredCriteria, ObservedFactsHash)` with predicates `lane_done`/`lane_tasks_completed`/`lane_supervision_pass` and a JSON converter that still reads M2-era plain lane-key strings — and `UnmetLaneWaits` derives dep waits with a fresh facts hash each re-judge. When a parked lane's predicate holds, `ClassifyParkedLanesAsync` moves it to `gate_review` and really calls that lane's planner as the gate reviewer (`BuildGatePrompt`: `Lane: {key}` header, `门控评审：`, per-task facts with criteria/status/result/evidence, latest `CriterionVerdict` JSON, and `ObservedFactsHash:`), instructing tighten-only `{"decision":"proceed|wait_more|escalate"}`. A `proceed` is accepted only if the observed hash is unchanged AND `GateCodeFactsHold` re-verifies the target lane in code (all tasks completed, every latest-round CriterionVerdict satisfied with non-empty evidence) — the model cannot override false facts; otherwise the gate is rejected as stale (`gate.review.rejected_stale`) and `EscalateLaneAsync` freezes just that lane (`lane.Escalated=true`), flips the run to `awaiting_user`, and emits `supervision.user_review.requested`. `wait_more` over an unchanged hash escalates too (`LastGateFactsHash` loop guard). Verdicts now land on the lane: `SuperviseLaneAsync` runs the supervisor when one lane is terminal while another lane still has live work under `[supervision] required_before_final`, mapping `verdict.CriterionVerdicts` onto `task.CriteriaVerdicts` (ReviewedBy=supervisor) so gates read real per-criterion evidence. `CriterionVerdictsHold` treats `RequiredCriteria=null` as check-all-verdicts and `[]` as completion-only (derived dep waits gate on completion alone; the gate's hard validation checks all). Event sequence per gate: `orchestration.lane_waiting` → `orchestration.gate_review` → `orchestration.gate_review.completed`. Test harness: `ScriptedChatClient` gained lane-aware routing (`WhenPlanner(lane, script)` per-lane scripts + `WhenGate`, `PlannerLaneCalls`/`GateCalls`/`GatePrompts` counters; gate calls are recognized by the `门控评审` marker before the planner branch so they never consume planner scripts). New E2E: `TwoLanes_AdvanceInParallelUnderSingleRunLease` (both lanes' workers run concurrently without a second run lease), `LaneGate_WaitingDoesNotFailRunAsInvalidTaskGraph`, `LaneGate_GateSequenceProceedsThroughWaitingReviewExecuting` (exact 3-event sequence, GateCalls==1, prompt content asserts), `GateReview_ModelProceedCannotOverrideFalseFacts` (supervisor pass with a false verdict → model proceeds → rejected_stale + awaiting_user). Honest gaps: budget items deferred to M4 (`max_agents_per_run` 8→16, `AgentInstanceRecord.LaneKey`, `max_lanes_per_run`/`max_tasks_per_lane` not yet enforced at dispatch); scenario-1 SSE `lane_opened` directive consumption deferred to M4; escalation-resume UX flow lands M4/M5; lease-owner persistence is not directly assertable at endpoint level (the engine delegates leasing to the coordinator/lifecycle layer); the orchestration endpoint's nodes remain event-rebuilt without a lane dimension (M6).
- **M4 meeting-authored orchestration port (2026-09-01, AgentFramework 86 / Api 163 green)**: the meeting agent can now land deferred user intent ("after it finishes, test and commit") as a governed lane on the target run. When `lanes_enabled` and the interaction targets a run, `GenerateInteractionResponseAsync` appends the `LANE_OPEN` protocol contract to the meeting instructions; the engine strips every `LANE_OPEN:` line from the model output (they never reach the user stream), validates the last one through the new `IOrchestrationDirectiveValidator` (Abstractions/Ports, implemented fail-closed in `DmaEA/Orchestration/`: verb whitelist LANE_OPEN/LANE_CLOSE/LANE_WAIT/LANE_STATUS_QUERY, `lanes_disabled`, duplicate/lane-budget, goal-or-title, task budget, duplicate task keys, in-lane-only dependencies, DFS cycle detection, wait-target existence, `tool_scope ⊆` frozen manifest incl. wildcard, and mutating-tool declarations require a `pre_authorization` reference — which M4 rejects as `preauthorization_unavailable` until M5 wires real consumption), and on acceptance persists a durable `run_directives` row (`kind="orchestration"`, idempotency key `directive:{target}:{source}:{sha256(payload)}`) via the new `ILifecycleManager.EnqueueRunDirectiveAsync` (tenant/workspace derived from the target run row). The target run's owner consumes pending orchestration directives beside the context-patch pass each tick (`ApplyPendingOrchestrationDirectivesAsync`), re-validates against the live checkpoint (duplicate lane and lane budget are authoritative here — admission-side validation runs on conservative facts), materializes accepted lanes (`ValidateAndMaterializeGraph` + `SyncLanes`, structured `LaneWait`s attached, `orchestration.lane_opened {lane_key, task_keys, waits}` event), pulls a `finalizing/done` checkpoint phase back to `executing` so a lane opened after the earlier lanes finished still executes, and marks rows `consumed`/`rejected`. Run-terminal drain fails closed for late orchestration directives (`run_terminal`) while keeping the M2 queued-interaction semantics. The dead `RuntimeAgentDefinition.Accepts/Emits` fields were deleted (zero writers, zero consumers); `Triggers` stays (real consumer in `OperationalTriggers`). `ClassifyTurn` was verified rather than changed: a deferred instruction with `target_run_id` already lands on the clarification channel, which is the intended meeting-only directive carrier. E2E `MeetingDirective_LaneOpenConsumedByTargetRun` runs the scenario-1 spine: mid-run user leaves saying "完成后测试并提交" → meeting turn queues the directive (user sees only a code-generated confirmation) → main lane finishes → lane `l2` opens, waits on `main`, executes its task, run completes with exactly 2 worker calls and no rejected directives. Validator invariants pinned by 8 facts including `DirectiveValidator_RejectsToolScopeWidening_AndMissingPreAuthorization`. Honest gaps: LANE_CLOSE/LANE_WAIT/LANE_STATUS_QUERY are protocol-validated but consumption rejects them as `verb_not_implemented` (landing with M5/M6); `pre_authorization` references are rejected until M5; admission-side lane facts are conservative (duplicate/budget enforced at consumption); the orchestration endpoint still has no lane projection (M6).
- **M5① long-park approval windows (2026-09-01, Api 182+1-known-flake green, incl. the 4 real-process TinadecTools tests)**: approval expiry is split into a decision window and an execution window (`Lifecycle/TinadecApprovalOptions.cs`, `TinadecApproval:DecisionWindowMinutes`/`ExecutionWindowMinutes`, both default 30, clamped 1–1440, bound in `LifecycleModuleRegistrar`). A pending approval whose decision window lapses no longer fails the tool call — `TryStartAsync` parks it: the approval row expires, the execution stays `awaiting_approval`, and an `approval.park_expired` event is appended for the engine/lane to escalate or re-approve (consumption is M4-leftover scope). An approved approval whose execution window lapses still fails closed (`approval_expired`, execution `failed`) before any tool runs; rows pre-dating the split keep the old hard-fail semantics through the `ExecutionWindowExpiresAt ?? ExpiresAt` fallback. Runs parked on `awaiting_user` are excluded from `CountActiveRunsAsync`, so waiting on a human decision no longer consumes the session's `MaxActiveRunsPerSession` admission budget (needed for the scenario-1 deferred lane). Tests: `ApprovalWindowTests` (4: park-with-event, execution-window hard-fail, legacy-row fallback, admission exemption). Honest gap: the engine does not yet consume `approval.park_expired` to escalate the lane; the `execution_window_expires_at` column is additive and reconciled by the schema bootstrapper.
- **M5④ auto-approve policy (2026-09-01, Governance 110 / Api 183 green)**: `Governance/AutoApproveOptions.cs` (`TinadecApproval:AutoApproveEnabled` default **false**, `AutoApproveRiskMax` default medium, `AutoApproveMaxPerRun` default 5, `HumanOnlyTools` = git_push/command_run/git_worktree_remove/mcp_invoke plus any id ending `_delete` or starting `delete_`, `PolicyVersion` const `auto-approve-v1`) arms a third decision source inside `GovernanceService.DecidePermissionCoreAsync`: when no delegation was supplied AND the caller lacks human authority, `TryAutoPolicyAsync` (inserted before the `unauthorized_approver` gate) may approve instead of deny — engaging only on `approve: true`, never for human-only tools or above-ceiling risk. Approved auto decisions reuse the exact human grant path (frozen boundaries re-evaluated, same grant/lease CAS), carry `DecisionSource="auto_policy"`, `ReasonCode="auto_policy_approved"` with the policy version in the reason, and blank both `DecidedBy*` columns so a policy decision can never masquerade as a person or agent; an `approval.auto_decided {policy_version, tool_id, risk, lane_key, budget_remaining}` lifecycle event is appended per decision. Budget exhaustion **escalates, not denies** (request returns to `awaiting_user` with `auto_policy_budget_exhausted` — a denied request is terminal and could never be human-decided afterwards); per-run budget counts prior `auto_policy` decisions, with run-less requests sharing the null-run pool. Delegation `RequireUserReview` semantics pass through untouched (the policy only engages in the no-delegation branch). Tests: `AutoApprovePolicyTests` (11: disabled-by-default pins `unauthorized_approver`, in-envelope approval, human-only list ×6, per-run budget escalation, RequireUserReview passthrough, lease-scope mismatch on a different claim). Honest gaps: the tool-approval chain (Lifecycle approvals minted by `ToolDispatcher`) has no auto-approve trigger yet — unattended runs today ride ② pre-authorization or ③ full-access; wiring ④ into that chain would need an `Abstractions` port since Lifecycle does not reference Governance (outside the plan's ④ text); `lane_key` in the event payload is always null until permission requests carry a lane dimension; the plan-level `*_delete` pattern was widened to also cover `delete_*` ids because this repo's delete tools are named `delete_file`-style.
- **M5 docs debt: approval-bypass reversal record (2026-09-01)**: the removed `FrozenRunConfiguration.cs` comment "deliberately has no approval bypass" is a deliberately overturned architecture decision (overturned by M5①–④, not an accidental deletion). Canonical record with rationale/compensating controls/residual risk lives in `docs/tinadec-core-product-definition.zh-CN.md` §10.5; the repo-root AGENTS.md carries the same record. In short — why: scenario-1 unattended lanes cannot terminate a frozen `awaiting_user` park, and the UI already offered the modes governance denied; compensating controls: frozen-manifest intersection + hash immutability, pre-authorization binding checks with one-shot nonce, auto-approve default-off with human-only list + risk ceiling + escalate-not-deny budget + blanked `DecidedBy*` + `approval.auto_decided` audit, execution-window fail-closed unchanged; residual risk: no human review point for unattended commits once enabled; the "no direct push to main" tool-layer guard landed the same day in TinadecTools (`ProtectedBranchGuard` — git_push refuses protected branches, shell command text parsed for `git push` refspec targets; text-level limits apply, user's own terminal ungoverned).

- **M8 unattended lane closure (2026-09-03, Governance 34 / AgentFramework 100 / Architecture 11 / Api 194+1-known-flake green, incl. the 3 real-process unattended E2E)**: scenario-1's deferred lane now runs unattended end to end. ① lane admission thaw: `OrchestrationDirectiveRules.FrozenPermissionMode` (validator no longer rejects `preauthorization_unavailable` unconditionally; a mutating lane needs a `pre_authorization` reference or a frozen unattended mode); admission-side validation was also re-anchored to the **target run's** frozen configuration (`FinalizeInteractionTextAsync` loads it; the interaction's own source run never freezes a manifest because only `new_task` turns do, so the source config rejected every tool-scoped directive with `tool_scope_widening`). ② lane_key pipe: `ToolExecutionRecord.LaneKey` + EF mapping, `ToolDispatchRequestDto.LaneKey` (`[JsonIgnore]`), pre-authorization grant matching relaxed to run-level-or-lane-exact with lane-bound grants preferred, approval events carry `lane_key`. ③ auto-policy port: `IToolApprovalAutoPolicy` (Abstractions) + `ToolApprovalAutoPolicy`/`AutoApprovePolicyRules` (pure rules, no store) consumed by `ToolApprovalCoordinator` after full-access and pre-authorization miss; per-run budget counts the caller's own `ApprovalDecisions` (reason=`auto_policy_approved`) — Governance's permission path keeps its own counter, the two budgets are deliberately separate; `approval.auto_decided` audit events. ④ park_expired consumption: `ToolExecutionStartDecision.ParkExpired` + `ToolDispatchResultDto.ParkExpired` (`[JsonIgnore]`) drive `EscalateLaneAsync` (freeze lane, `awaiting_user`). ⑤ per-lane planner: goal-only `LANE_OPEN` directives (`tasks` optional) open the lane in `planning`, spawn a lane-tagged task-planner instance (`RuntimeAgentSeed.LaneKey`, `LanePlannerIds`, `lane_planning`/`lane_planned` events, `Lane: {key}` instruction marker), gate review routes to that planner; spawn budget 8→16 across three toml syncs. ⑥ real-chain E2E `UnattendedLaneEndToEndTests` (3 `[RequiresTinadecToolsFact]`: full-access / pre-authorization / auto-policy) — a mid-run goal-only directive opens lane l2 whose planner derives a shell+git_commit task graph, and the mutating tools release without a human through the real TinadecTools child process into a real temp git repo (`feature.txt` written, exactly one "M8 unattended commit"). **Two product gaps the E2E exposed and closed in the same change**: (a) admission validated against the source run's empty manifest (fixed above); (b) the three unattended release paths all lived downstream of the PDP permission request, which parks `awaiting_user` whenever no capability grant matches — real dispatches never reached the approval mint. The PDP now releases unattended calls keyed on the frozen permission mode (`GovernanceService.RequestPermissionAsync`: `full-access` → run-scoped grant+lease reason `full_access_auto_grant`; `auto-approve` + shared auto-approve rule engagement → `auto_policy_released`, no budget spent here so the approval layer stays the single consumer; `ask`/null parks exactly as before, M5④ decide-path semantics untouched; `DecidedByPrincipalId` is emptied on mode/policy releases so they never masquerade as a human). Pre-authorization now also mints one run-scoped capability grant per tool (`ControlPlaneService.CreatePreAuthorization`) so the PDP grant search hits directly — the record stays the consumption authority (max_uses, one per call, CAS at the mint); the grant's own use budget only covers the dispatcher's lease-use reservation (amplified by remaining tool rounds) and is not the control. `NewLease` now binds the lease to the requesting subject (`command/request.SubjectAgentInstanceId`) instead of copying the grant's — for agent-bound grants equivalent, for the agent-null pre-authorization envelope it fixes `lease_subject_mismatch` at consumption. - **Workspace snapshot/defaults surfaces (2026-08-22)**: `IWorkspaceSnapshotProvider` has filesystem and safe-argument-list Git implementations; `IWorkspaceSnapshotService` persists provider-neutral snapshots plus a separate `session_metadata_snapshots` projection. Git captures HEAD/ref, index/tree, worktree, binary patches, untracked/deleted/conflict paths; restore validates current state and is idempotent. `UserToolActionService` and `ToolDispatcher` capture high-risk write snapshots before permission/action approval; snapshot failure blocks until a current-user one-time override records a non-reversible audit mark. `WorkspaceDefaults` has tenant/workspace-scoped draft/publish/archive handlers with ETag/If-Match checks. SQLite and PostgreSQL both receive the schema and content is stored through the immutable ContentStore.
- **User tool governance (2026-08-22)**: `UserToolAction` is a durable action outside the run/task/agent graph. Core derives the principal from tenant context and freezes parameters, Tool Provider protocol/manifest identity, the complete v2 descriptor (schema/risk/mutation/approval/retry semantics), and snapshot bindings. Every resume verifies the live manifest, descriptor, confirmation fields, and parameters before consuming authorization or calling the provider. A serialized startup recovery pass idempotently advances decided waiting actions, uses an action-status CAS to prevent concurrent provider calls, and converts restart-orphaned `running` actions to `outcome_unknown` without replay. It currently scans only `ITenantContextAccessor.Current`, which is sufficient for the local single-workspace host; cloud multi-tenant recovery still requires a tenant scheduler and distributed claim. The action shares PDP/lease/ActionApproval with agent execution, stores nonce hashes plus protected material references, and never emits nonce material in DTOs or Gateway responses; invalid approval binding, schema/manifest drift, lease expiry/revocation, and unknown external outcomes fail closed. Snapshot override and remote push persist `non_reversible` plus public compensation guidance.
- **模型与智能体控制面重构 (2026-08-27)**: per-agent model strategy is `inherit|route|fixed` only — `model_routes` carry ordered `model_route_candidates` (`position`, migration `202608270002_ModelRoutesV2`); `fixed` binds `provider_instance_id` + optional `model` (null allowed for CLI/ACP provider instances); the legacy parent-select/cli/acp strategy kinds and the profile write path are gone (migration `202608270004` drops those tables). `IAgentModelResolver` (`Runtime/AgentModelResolver.cs`) is the single resolution + attribution authority: every chat invocation persists a `model_invocations` row (call_id/attempt, `strategy_source`, route + provider version ids, model/protocol, `fallback_position`, status, token usage) indexed per run/agent/mode/provider (`202608270003_ModelInvocations`). Sessions store a structured `meeting_model_override` (`provider_instance_id` + `model`, `202608270005_StructuredMeetingModelOverride`), replacing the old free-text model + split provider columns. Agent definitions carry `source_kind` (`bootstrap|pack|custom|missing_reference`), `source_key`, and `managed` (unique per workspace, `202608270001_AgentModelDirectory`); `mode_nodes` gained `model_strategy_override`; `Runtime/BootstrapAgentDirectory.cs` seeds the bootstrap directory. New endpoints in `ModelAgentControlEndpoints.cs`: `POST /api/v1/model-resolution/preview` (what-if chain without persisting), `GET /api/v1/model-references` (agent/mode/route/recent-invocation back-references for a provider + model), `GET /api/v1/model-invocations` (cursor-paged attribution log); `GET /api/v1/agents` in `AgentConfigurationEndpoints.cs` returns the full directory projection (source identity, mode usages, effective strategy preview, recent invocation). The legacy catalog route and the standalone `application-modes` projection were deleted — no compatibility aliases. SQLite keeps every `DateTimeOffset` ordering client-side after materialization.
